topics.name: ICP Physiology and Herniation
topics.blurb: Intracranial pressure mechanics, compliance, perfusion pressure, and herniation syndromes.

topics.name: Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
topics.blurb: Autoregulation, CO2 reactivity, ischemic thresholds, and flow-metabolism coupling.

topics.name: CSF Dynamics
topics.blurb: CSF production, circulation, absorption, and the physiology of hydrocephalus.

topics.name: Cellular Neurophysiology and Electrophysiology
topics.blurb: Excitability, synaptic transmission, the blood-brain barrier, edema, and electrophysiology.

topics.name: Neurological Examination
topics.blurb: Coma scoring, cranial nerve, motor-sensory, brainstem, and localization examination.

topics.name: Neuroimaging Fundamentals
topics.blurb: CT, MRI sequences, angiography, perfusion, and imaging safety for neurosurgery.

topics.name: Neurosurgical Pharmacology
topics.blurb: Osmotherapy, antiepileptics, steroids, anticoagulation, sedation, and CNS antibiotics.

topics.name: Perioperative and Intraoperative Foundations
topics.blurb: Positioning, hemostasis, neuromonitoring, prophylaxis, anesthesia, and CSF diversion.

topics.name: Neurology for Neurosurgeons
topics.blurb: Demyelinating, neuromuscular, degenerative, headache, seizure, and infectious neurology.

topics.name: Evidence-Based Medicine and Outcomes
topics.blurb: Trial appraisal, study design, biostatistics, evidence levels, and outcome scales.

concepts.name: Monro-Kellie doctrine
concepts.blurb: Fixed cranial volume means any increase in brain, blood, or CSF must be offset or ICP rises.
acgme: CSF Physiology and Intracranial Compliance - Monroe-Kellie Doctrine

concepts.name: Normal ICP values and measurement
concepts.blurb: Normal adult ICP is 7-15 mmHg supine; sustained pressure above 20-22 mmHg is pathologic.

concepts.name: Pressure-volume curve and compliance
concepts.blurb: Exponential pressure-volume relationship: compliance is high until the elastance knee, then small volumes spike ICP.
acgme: CSF Physiology and Intracranial Compliance - Monroe-Kellie Doctrine

concepts.name: ICP waveforms (P1/P2/P3)
concepts.blurb: Normal ICP pulse shows P1 greater than P2 greater than P3; P2 rising above P1 signals falling compliance.

concepts.name: Lundberg and plateau waves
concepts.blurb: Lundberg A (plateau) waves indicate exhausted compliance and impending herniation; B waves reflect vasomotor instability.

concepts.name: CPP calculation and targets
concepts.blurb: CPP equals MAP minus ICP; cerebral perfusion depends on this gradient, targeted around 60-70 mmHg after injury.
acgme: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure - CPP MAP - ICP Targets and Optimization

concepts.name: Cushing response
concepts.blurb: Hypertension, bradycardia, and irregular respiration form the triad signaling critically raised ICP and brainstem compression.

concepts.name: Herniation syndromes
concepts.blurb: Uncal, central, subfalcine, and tonsillar herniation produce predictable progressive brainstem and vascular compromise.
acgme: Transtentorial Uncal and Tonsillar Herniation - Recognition and Management

concepts.name: ICP treatment thresholds
concepts.blurb: Treat sustained ICP above 20-22 mmHg with a tiered protocol while defending CPP around 60-70 mmHg.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: ICP monitoring methods
concepts.blurb: EVD measures pressure and drains CSF; parenchymal monitors only measure but carry lower infection risk.
acgme: ICP Monitoring - Parenchymal Monitor Placement and Interpretation

concepts.name: Cerebral autoregulation
concepts.blurb: Autoregulation holds cerebral blood flow constant across MAP of roughly 50-150 mmHg via myogenic arteriolar tone.
acgme: Cerebral Autoregulation and Cerebral Blood Flow Regulation

concepts.name: CO2 reactivity of cerebral vessels
concepts.blurb: Cerebral blood flow changes about 3-4 percent per mmHg PaCO2; hyperventilation lowers flow by vasoconstriction.
acgme: Cerebral Autoregulation and Cerebral Blood Flow Regulation

concepts.name: Ischemic CBF thresholds
concepts.blurb: CBF below 20 mL/100g/min causes electrical failure; below 10 causes membrane failure and infarction.

concepts.name: Normal cerebral blood flow values
concepts.blurb: Global CBF averages 50 mL/100g/min; gray matter near 80, white matter near 20, about 15 percent of cardiac output.

concepts.name: Flow-metabolism coupling
concepts.blurb: Flow-metabolism coupling matches CBF to local CMRO2; uncoupling produces ischemia or hyperemia.

concepts.name: Ischemic penumbra
concepts.blurb: The penumbra is hypoperfused but salvageable tissue surrounding the infarct core and the target of reperfusion.

concepts.name: Cerebral steal and luxury perfusion
concepts.blurb: Maximally dilated ischemic vessels cannot respond; vasodilators divert flow away while luxury perfusion follows reperfusion.

concepts.name: Oxygen and glucose substrate delivery
concepts.blurb: Oxygen and glucose delivery depend on blood flow and content; the brain holds minimal energy reserve.

concepts.name: CSF production and circulation
concepts.blurb: Choroid plexus secretes about 500 mL/day circulating from ventricles to subarachnoid space; total volume near 150 mL.
acgme: CSF Pathway - Production (Choroid Plexus) Circulation Absorption (Arachnoid Villi)

concepts.name: CSF absorption pathways
concepts.blurb: CSF is absorbed at arachnoid granulations into venous sinuses, with glymphatic and lymphatic routes also contributing.
acgme: CSF Pathway - Production (Choroid Plexus) Circulation Absorption (Arachnoid Villi)

concepts.name: Normal CSF composition
concepts.blurb: Normal CSF is clear with 0-5 WBC, glucose near 60 percent of serum, protein 15-45 mg/dL, opening pressure 6-20 cmH2O.
acgme: Meningitis and Encephalitis - Diagnosis Empiric Treatment and LP Interpretation

concepts.name: Communicating vs obstructive hydrocephalus
concepts.blurb: Obstructive hydrocephalus blocks flow within the ventricles; communicating impairs absorption with patent ventricular outflow.

concepts.name: Hydrocephalus physiology
concepts.blurb: Hydrocephalus is CSF accumulation from imbalance of production, absorption, or flow, enlarging ventricles and raising ICP.

concepts.name: Normal pressure hydrocephalus physiology
concepts.blurb: NPH causes gait apraxia, dementia, and incontinence with normal pressure and ventriculomegaly responsive to shunting.
acgme: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus - Triad Tap Test and Shunting

concepts.name: Neuronal excitability and action potentials
concepts.blurb: Resting potential and voltage-gated sodium and potassium channels generate and propagate the action potential.
acgme: Neuronal Physiology - Action Potentials Synaptic Transmission Receptors

concepts.name: Synaptic transmission
concepts.blurb: Calcium-triggered neurotransmitter release activates postsynaptic receptors producing excitatory or inhibitory potentials.
acgme: Neuronal Physiology - Action Potentials Synaptic Transmission Receptors

concepts.name: Neurotransmitter systems
concepts.blurb: Glutamate, GABA, dopamine, acetylcholine, and monoamine systems mediate distinct CNS functions and drug targets.
acgme: Neuronal Physiology - Action Potentials Synaptic Transmission Receptors

concepts.name: Blood-brain barrier
concepts.blurb: Tight-junction endothelium restricts CNS entry; breakdown produces contrast enhancement and vasogenic edema.
acgme: Blood-Brain Barrier - Structure Function and Pharmacological Implications

concepts.name: Cerebral edema (vasogenic vs cytotoxic)
concepts.blurb: Vasogenic edema from BBB breakdown is extracellular; cytotoxic edema from cell-membrane failure is intracellular.
acgme: CNS Injury Responses - Vasogenic vs Cytotoxic Edema Excitotoxicity

concepts.name: Excitotoxicity
concepts.blurb: Ischemia floods synapses with glutamate, driving calcium influx, mitochondrial failure, and neuronal death.
acgme: CNS Injury Responses - Vasogenic vs Cytotoxic Edema Excitotoxicity

concepts.name: Cortical spreading depolarization
concepts.blurb: A propagating wave of depolarization and metabolic stress worsens ischemia in injured brain and may link to aura.

concepts.name: Glial cell biology
concepts.blurb: Astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia, and ependyma support, myelinate, defend, and line the CNS.
acgme: Glial Cell Biology - Astrocytes Oligodendrocytes Microglia Ependyma

concepts.name: Axonal transport and Wallerian degeneration
concepts.blurb: Axonal injury causes anterograde Wallerian degeneration; axonal transport sustains the distal axon.
acgme: Axonal Transport and Wallerian Degeneration

concepts.name: EEG basics
concepts.blurb: EEG records cortical rhythms (delta, theta, alpha, beta) for seizures, encephalopathy, and burst suppression.

concepts.name: Evoked potentials
concepts.blurb: Evoked potentials test pathway integrity: SSEP for dorsal columns, MEP for corticospinal, BAER for auditory brainstem.
acgme: Neurophysiology of Intraoperative Monitoring (SSEP MEP EMG ABR)

concepts.name: Myelination and conduction
concepts.blurb: Myelin enables saltatory conduction; oligodendrocytes myelinate centrally and Schwann cells peripherally.

concepts.name: Glasgow Coma Scale
concepts.blurb: The Glasgow Coma Scale scores eye, verbal, and motor responses from 3 to 15 to grade consciousness.
acgme: TBI Classification - Mild Moderate Severe (GCS) and Marshall or Rotterdam CT Score

concepts.name: Cranial nerve examination
concepts.blurb: Systematic testing of cranial nerves I-XII localizes brainstem and skull base lesions.
acgme: Cranial Nerves I-XII - Anatomy Nuclei and Clinical Syndromes

concepts.name: Motor and sensory examination
concepts.blurb: Graded strength testing, sensory mapping, and reflexes localize lesions along the neuraxis.
acgme: Functional Systems - Motor Sensory Visual Language Vestibular Pathways

concepts.name: Brainstem reflexes
concepts.blurb: Pupillary, corneal, oculocephalic, oculovestibular, and gag reflexes test brainstem integrity by level.

concepts.name: Coma examination
concepts.blurb: Structured coma assessment uses GCS, brainstem reflexes, motor response, and respiratory pattern to localize.

concepts.name: Pupillary light reflex pathway
concepts.blurb: The light reflex runs CN II afferent to CN III efferent; a blown pupil signals uncal herniation.
acgme: Neuro-Ophthalmology - Visual Field Defects Pupillary Reflexes Diplopia Localization

concepts.name: Spinal cord syndrome exam patterns
concepts.blurb: Brown-Sequard, central cord, anterior cord, and posterior cord syndromes produce distinct exam patterns.
acgme: Spinal Cord Anatomy - Tracts (Dorsal Columns Spinothalamic CST) Laminae

concepts.name: Reflex grading and UMN vs LMN
concepts.blurb: Deep tendon reflex grading and pathologic signs distinguish upper from lower motor neuron lesions.

concepts.name: Cerebellar examination
concepts.blurb: Tests for dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, ataxia, and nystagmus localize cerebellar dysfunction.

concepts.name: Cortical localization signs
concepts.blurb: Aphasia, neglect, apraxia, and visual field cuts localize cortical lesions by lobe and hemisphere.
acgme: Cerebral Lobes - Functional Anatomy and Localization

concepts.name: NIH Stroke Scale
concepts.blurb: The NIH Stroke Scale quantifies stroke deficit severity and guides reperfusion decisions and prognosis.

concepts.name: Brain death examination
concepts.blurb: Brain death requires coma, absent brainstem reflexes, and a positive apnea test off confounders, with ancillary tests as needed.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Gait and stance examination
concepts.blurb: Gait and Romberg testing screen for motor, cerebellar, sensory, and frontal disorders.

concepts.name: CT basics and Hounsfield density
concepts.blurb: Hounsfield density distinguishes blood, bone, edema, and CSF on noncontrast CT for emergent reads.
acgme: Non-Contrast CT Head Interpretation - Hemorrhage Mass Hydrocephalus

concepts.name: MRI sequences
concepts.blurb: T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, SWI, and post-gadolinium sequences each highlight specific tissue and pathology.
acgme: Brain MRI Sequences - T1 T2 FLAIR DWI SWI T1Gad - Clinical Application

concepts.name: Catheter angiography basics
concepts.blurb: Catheter DSA is the gold standard for cerebrovascular anatomy, aneurysms, AVMs, and dynamic flow.
acgme: Cerebral Angiography Interpretation - Normal Anatomy and Pathological Findings

concepts.name: Diffusion restriction and ADC
concepts.blurb: Diffusion restriction (bright DWI, dark ADC) marks acute infarct, abscess, and hypercellular tumor.
acgme: Brain MRI Sequences - T1 T2 FLAIR DWI SWI T1Gad - Clinical Application

concepts.name: Susceptibility imaging (SWI/GRE)
concepts.blurb: SWI and GRE detect blood products, calcium, and microbleeds through magnetic susceptibility blooming.
acgme: Brain MRI Sequences - T1 T2 FLAIR DWI SWI T1Gad - Clinical Application

concepts.name: CTA and CT perfusion
concepts.blurb: CTA maps vessels while CT perfusion estimates infarct core and penumbra to guide thrombectomy selection.
acgme: CT Angiography and CT Perfusion - Stroke and Vascular Pathology Interpretation

concepts.name: Contrast enhancement patterns
concepts.blurb: Gadolinium and iodinated contrast enhance where the BBB breaks down, revealing tumor, infection, and inflammation.

concepts.name: Advanced MRI (spectroscopy, perfusion, fMRI)
concepts.blurb: MR spectroscopy, perfusion, and functional MRI add metabolic, hemodynamic, and eloquent-cortex mapping data.
acgme: Advanced MRI - Spectroscopy Perfusion Functional MRI in Neurosurgery

concepts.name: DTI and tractography
concepts.blurb: Diffusion tensor imaging reconstructs white matter tracts for surgical planning near eloquent pathways.
acgme: White Matter Tracts - Corticospinal Corticobulbar Arcuate Fasciculus and MR Tractography

concepts.name: CT myelography
concepts.blurb: CT myelography injects intrathecal contrast to outline the thecal sac when MRI is contraindicated or inconclusive.

concepts.name: Nuclear imaging (SPECT/PET)
concepts.blurb: PET and SPECT image metabolism and perfusion for tumor grading, recurrence, and epilepsy localization.
acgme: Nuclear Imaging - SPECT and PET in Neuro-Oncology and Epilepsy

concepts.name: Radiation and contrast safety
concepts.blurb: ALARA principles, contrast nephropathy, and gadolinium risks govern safe neuroimaging and fluoroscopy use.

concepts.name: Plain spine radiography
concepts.blurb: Plain radiographs assess spinal alignment, instability, fractures, deformity, and hardware position.
acgme: Plain Radiography of the Spine - Trauma Deformity Hardware Assessment

concepts.name: Intraoperative ultrasound
concepts.blurb: Real-time intraoperative ultrasound localizes lesions and assesses resection in brain and spine surgery.
acgme: Intraoperative Ultrasound - Brain and Spine Applications

concepts.name: Osmotherapy (mannitol vs hypertonic saline)
concepts.blurb: Mannitol and hypertonic saline create osmotic gradients to draw water from brain tissue and reduce ICP.
acgme: Osmotherapy - Mannitol vs Hypertonic Saline - Mechanisms and Targets

concepts.name: Antiepileptic drugs
concepts.blurb: AEDs such as levetiracetam, phenytoin, and valproate suppress seizures via sodium, calcium, or GABA mechanisms.
acgme: Antiepileptic Drug Pharmacology - Mechanisms and Interactions

concepts.name: Anticoagulation reversal
concepts.blurb: Reverse warfarin with PCC and vitamin K, heparin with protamine, and DOACs with andexanet or idarucizumab.
acgme: Coagulopathy Reversal in Neurosurgery - Warfarin NOAC Antiplatelet Reversal

concepts.name: Dexamethasone for peritumoral edema
concepts.blurb: Dexamethasone reduces vasogenic peritumoral edema by stabilizing the blood-brain barrier; it does not treat cytotoxic edema.
acgme: Peritumoral Edema - Dexamethasone and Medical Management

concepts.name: Antiplatelet agents
concepts.blurb: Aspirin, clopidogrel, and ticagrelor inhibit platelet aggregation; key for stenting and ischemic prevention.

concepts.name: Anticoagulants
concepts.blurb: Warfarin, heparins, and DOACs interrupt the coagulation cascade at distinct points with different reversal needs.

concepts.name: Sedatives and analgesics
concepts.blurb: Propofol, dexmedetomidine, fentanyl, and midazolam balance sedation and analgesia against rapid neuro reassessment.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Neuromuscular blocking agents
concepts.blurb: Depolarizing and non-depolarizing paralytics enable intubation and surgery but abolish the motor exam and MEPs.

concepts.name: Vasopressors in neurosurgery
concepts.blurb: Norepinephrine, phenylephrine, and vasopressin raise MAP to defend CPP and treat neurogenic shock.

concepts.name: CNS-penetrating antibiotics
concepts.blurb: CNS-penetrating antibiotics drive prophylaxis and empiric coverage for meningitis, ventriculitis, and abscess.
acgme: Sepsis and CNS Infection in the ICU - Meningitis Ventriculitis Abscess

concepts.name: Neuro-oncology chemotherapy basics
concepts.blurb: Temozolomide, bevacizumab, and nitrosoureas treat CNS tumors; BBB penetration and MGMT status guide use.

concepts.name: Nimodipine
concepts.blurb: Nimodipine, a calcium channel blocker, improves outcomes after aneurysmal SAH by reducing delayed cerebral ischemia.

concepts.name: Surgical hemostasis
concepts.blurb: Mechanical, thermal, and topical agents control bleeding; meticulous hemostasis prevents postoperative hematoma.

concepts.name: Surgical positioning
concepts.blurb: Positioning optimizes exposure and venous drainage while preventing pressure, nerve, and eye injury.

concepts.name: Intraoperative neuromonitoring
concepts.blurb: Intraoperative SSEP, MEP, EMG, and EEG monitor neural integrity to prevent surgical injury.
acgme: Neurophysiology of Intraoperative Monitoring (SSEP MEP EMG ABR)

concepts.name: VTE prophylaxis decisions
concepts.blurb: Mechanical and chemical VTE prophylaxis balance thrombosis risk against postoperative intracranial hemorrhage timing.
acgme: DVT or PE Prophylaxis in Neurosurgery - Timing Risk Stratification

concepts.name: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis
concepts.blurb: Timely preoperative antibiotics reduce surgical site infection; redosing depends on case length and blood loss.
acgme: Surgical Site Infection in Neurosurgery - Prevention Diagnosis and Treatment

concepts.name: Wound healing and closure
concepts.blurb: Layered closure, vascularity, nutrition, and infection control determine scalp and spinal wound healing.

concepts.name: Anesthesia for neurosurgery
concepts.blurb: Neuroanesthesia controls CO2, blood pressure, and brain relaxation while preserving neuromonitoring signals.

concepts.name: Awake craniotomy anesthesia
concepts.blurb: Asleep-awake-asleep technique with scalp blocks enables intraoperative language and motor mapping.

concepts.name: Positioning complications
concepts.blurb: Malpositioning causes peripheral nerve palsy, pressure ulcers, postoperative vision loss, and compartment syndrome.

concepts.name: Venous air embolism
concepts.blurb: Sitting-position surgery risks venous air embolism; detect via precordial Doppler and a falling end-tidal CO2.

concepts.name: External ventricular drain placement
concepts.blurb: An external ventricular drain placed via Kocher's point both monitors ICP and drains CSF.
acgme: Ventriculostomy (EVD) Placement - Kocher Point Technique and Complications

concepts.name: Lumbar drain placement
concepts.blurb: Lumbar drains divert CSF for leaks, hydrocephalus trials, and aneurysm or aortic surgery cord protection.
acgme: Lumbar Drain Placement - Technique Indications and Complications

concepts.name: Demyelinating disease
concepts.blurb: MS, ADEM, and PML demyelinate the CNS and can mimic tumors, complicating the surgical differential.
acgme: Multiple Sclerosis and Demyelinating Disease - Neurosurgical Implications

concepts.name: Neuromuscular disease
concepts.blurb: ALS, myasthenia gravis, and Guillain-Barre affect the motor unit; recognition prevents perioperative respiratory disaster.
acgme: Neuromuscular Disease - ALS Myasthenia GBS - Neurosurgical Awareness

concepts.name: Dementia syndromes
concepts.blurb: Alzheimer, frontotemporal, and Lewy body dementias differ clinically and must be distinguished from reversible NPH.
acgme: Dementia Syndromes (Alzheimer FTD LBD) - Neurosurgical Differential

concepts.name: Headache syndromes and red flags
concepts.blurb: Differentiate primary headaches from thunderclap and red-flag presentations demanding neurosurgical workup.
acgme: Headache Differential Diagnosis - Migraine Cluster Thunderclap - Red Flags

concepts.name: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension
concepts.blurb: IIH presents with elevated ICP, papilledema, and headache without a mass, often in obese young women.

concepts.name: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
concepts.blurb: SIH from a CSF leak causes orthostatic headache and diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement on imaging.

concepts.name: Seizure classification
concepts.blurb: ILAE classifies seizures by onset (focal, generalized, unknown) and awareness, guiding workup and therapy.
acgme: Seizure Classification and Pathophysiology (ILAE 2017)

concepts.name: Status epilepticus
concepts.blurb: Status epilepticus is prolonged or recurrent seizures requiring escalating benzodiazepines, AEDs, and anesthetics.
acgme: Status Epilepticus - Recognition and Treatment Protocol

concepts.name: Functional neurological disorder
concepts.blurb: Functional neurological disorder produces internally inconsistent deficits; recognition avoids unnecessary surgery.

concepts.name: CNS infection (meningitis, encephalitis, abscess)
concepts.blurb: Meningitis, encephalitis, and abscess present with fever and deficits; LP and imaging guide empiric therapy.
acgme: Meningitis and Encephalitis - Diagnosis Empiric Treatment and LP Interpretation

concepts.name: Neuropathology of neurodegeneration
concepts.blurb: Protein-aggregation pathology underlies Alzheimer, Parkinson, ALS, and CTE neurodegeneration.
acgme: Neuropathology of Degenerative Diseases - Alzheimer Parkinson ALS CTE

concepts.name: Clinical trial interpretation
concepts.blurb: Critically appraise randomized trials for validity, effect size, and applicability before changing practice.

concepts.name: Study design hierarchy
concepts.blurb: RCT, cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional designs sit in a hierarchy of bias and strength of inference.

concepts.name: Outcome scales (mRS, GOS, KPS)
concepts.blurb: mRS, GOS, and KPS quantify functional outcome and are the common currency of neurosurgical trials.

concepts.name: Levels of evidence and guideline grades
concepts.blurb: Evidence and guideline grades rank recommendation strength from expert opinion to meta-analysis of RCTs.

concepts.name: Biostatistics basics
concepts.blurb: P-values, confidence intervals, NNT, sensitivity, and specificity translate trial data into clinical decisions.

concepts.name: Bias and confounding
concepts.blurb: Selection, measurement, and confounding biases threaten validity; randomization and adjustment mitigate them.
